messages:
maya (support): FYI getting multiple customer escalations — hosted API returning 504/5xx and client timeouts between 15:10-15:40 UTC. Customers report p95 spikes and some request retries. Stack traces show queue timeouts. Posting top-level metrics and a few screenshots.

lucas (oncall): copying dashboards now. Which tenants? any region skew?

maya (support): Tenants: acme-inc (us-west1), brightdoc (eu-west1), and one smaller tenant in us-east1. All on hosted-prod / model v1. No config change from customers. Happened right after a deploy at 15:05 (deploy-bot shows rollout complete).

anya (eng-runtime): pulling queue depth + batcher backlog. Initial read: continuous-batcher backlog jumped at 15:07 and dequeue rate dropped. Looks like kv-cache spin or batcher stall. attaching quick logs.

sre-bot: Metric highlights: request_queue_depth (hosted-prod) p99 -> 7800 at 15:12. continuous_batcher.backlog_count -> 4200. dequeue_rate dropped ~30%.

kevin (sre): can someone paste the batcher pod logs grep for ERR/timeout? running: kubectl -n hosted-prod logs -l app=batcher --tail=200

anya (eng-runtime): snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T15:11:58Z] batcher.cpp: enqueue request id=... queue_len=6123
[2026-03-17T15:12:00Z] batcher.cpp: trying to assemble batch, kvcache_miss=312
[2026-03-17T15:12:01Z] batcher.cpp: WARN slow-dequeue, dequeue_ms=2040
[2026-03-17T15:12:03Z] runtime.cpp: error: request deadline exceeded while waiting in queue
```

maya (support): customers are seeing 504s and retry storms. I've told them we're investigating and to hold off on retries for 20m.

lucas (oncall): immediate mitigation options: 1) raise request_queue_depth limit for hosted-prod 2) temporarily disable continuous batching 3) scale up batcher replicas 4) route a subset of traffic to fallback model variant (lower memory but faster dequeue). Any preferences?

anya (eng-runtime): quick test: disabling continuous batching in staging reduced backlog by 60% in <2m. For prod we can flip a runtime flag via config service: PATCH /v1/runtime/configs/hosted-prod {"continuous_batching": false}.

kevin (sre): I'll scale batcher + apply config. Doing `kubectl scale deployment/batcher --replicas=12 -n hosted-prod` now. Also increasing queue depth from 8k -> 12k on the gateway. Patch config in 30s.

sre-bot: action: scaled batcher replicas to 12 (deployment/batcher) — rollout started.

lucas (oncall): maya please send templated note to affected customers: "we observed request queue saturation causing intermittent 504s; mitigation in progress, expected reduced errors in 10-15m". Confirm when sent.

maya (support): Message sent to acme & brightdoc + support ticket links. Told them rollback not required but we're disabling batching and scaling.

anya (eng-runtime): applied runtime config: continuous_batching=false for hosted-prod (audit id cfg-7642). Also increased gateway queue_depth_limit to 12000 (applied via infra-config). Monitoring now.

sre-bot: system: gateway.queue_depth now 11987 -> 4300 over 6m. continuous_batcher.backlog_count dropping.

kevin (sre): dequeue rate back up, p95 request latency improving. I'm seeing fewer 5xx. rolling restart of older batcher pods finishing.

maya (support): customer acme confirms reduced 504s. brightdoc reports improved latency. Closing support escalations after monitoring 30m.

lucas (oncall): post-incident checklist: capture timeline, config changes (continuous_batching=false, queue_limit 12k), deploy that preceded incident (deploy-2026-03-17-14:58), batcher replica scale change. Create incident ticket and schedule postmortem with eng-runtime + sres.

anya (eng-runtime): root-cause hypothesis: deploy introduced a kernel-level scheduling change in batcher that increased nv12 kvcache misses leading to slower dequeue and cascading queue saturation. Will run a repro in staging and revert conservative batching optimization if repro matches. Adding feature-flag coverage to catch this in canary next time.

maya (support): adding public update to customers that mitigations applied and we're working on long-term fix.

lucas (oncall): thanks everyone. tagging for follow-up: @anya please own the postmortem, @kevin validate scaling/autoscaler thresholds, @maya draft customer follow-up. I'll leave the incident open until 18:00 UTC for postmortem notes.

kevin (sre): noted. saving logs and metrics to incident/3302468100. 

sre-bot: incident state -> monitoring.

(Reaction: :thumbsup: from maya, lucas, anya)
